note: The setup step table is the single source of ordering and source/investigator applicability. PDF preparation uses the host visual reader; no OCR or text bundle is required. System instructions are English; the setup assistant speaks the player language.

templates.unknown_step: There is no step named {step}. Available steps: {available}. Next: {next}
templates.needs_unmet: {step} is not available yet: finish {missing} first. Next: {next}
templates.already_done: {step} is already done (receipt {receipt}); it is not repeated. Next: {next}
templates.all_done: Setup is complete and the campaign is ready. Open the table: {launch}

starter.description: one of campaign.list's starter names (kernel.hello content.modules)

module.description: an id from module.list with status: installed -- an already-built book; preparation reuses its material and settles this campaign's opening

pdf.description: the original local PDF path; the host will read its pages visually

lines.do: Ask the player to pick a starter (the list from kernel.hello), an already-installed module (module.list, status: installed), or to give an original PDF path.
lines.next: Choose the source: name a starter, name an installed module, or give an original PDF path.

module_id.description: a previously registered module, if available

start_scene.description: an authored opening chosen after candidates were returned

lines.do: Prepare the chosen PDF or reuse the selected module. For multiple authored openings, match the player intent to the candidate summaries and select one before creating the campaign.
lines.next: Prepare the chosen PDF with prepare-module; if reading is still in progress, wait for the existing job rather than starting another.

module.description: starter id, or the module id source preparation returned (carried automatically)

play_language.description: BCP-47 tag of the language the keeper plays in: zh-Hans | en (default zh-Hans); the kernel writes nothing in it

lines.do: campaign.create: status setting_up; a starter is registered into the module store at the same time.
lines.next: Create the campaign: give a campaign id (and an optional title).

name.description: as the player said it, stored verbatim

occupation.description: an id from setup.occupations (the model maps the player's concept to it)

concept.description: optional, the player's one line, stored verbatim

seed.description: optional; rolled characteristics are reproducible from it

era.description: optional override of the module's era for the skill sheet and finance tables

allocation.description: optional occupation-point policy: spread | fill (default from this step's allocation block)

defaults.source_note: Chargen defaults are setup policy, not rulebook numbers: 27 sits in the 20-39 bracket (one EDU improvement check, no reductions) and quick_fire needs no dice.

allocation.source_note: Occupation-point policy (#21), content not code. spread: walk the occupation's skill list in the book's order, raising every entry to tiers[0], then tiers[1], then the starting cap (skills.json guided_creation_policy.starting_skill_cap); an entry the kernel cannot name (a rulebook choice such as 'any one other skill' or a group such as 'Firearms') is reserved the tier's value as unspent for the table's development family instead of the points piling onto the four skills it can name. fill: the earlier one-point round-robin over the resolvable entries only, kept as an option. The tiers are a table-feel choice (a rounded investigator over four maxed skills), not rulebook numbers.

formulas.source_note: Keeper Rulebook Chapter 3, personal interest skill points = INT x 2 (investigator-create-contract.json skill_budget description).

interest_pool.source_note: Keeper Rulebook Chapter 3: no points may be put into Cthulhu Mythos at creation; Credit Rating is set from the occupation's range.

lines.do: Ask only for a name and an occupation concept; map the concept to an occupation id with setup.occupations; the kernel derives every number.
lines.next: Create the investigator: tell me the name and the kind of person you want to play.

lines.do: investigator.list returns every card in the investigator library (name, occupation, era, HP/SAN, last campaign and turn, newest first); read it out and let the player choose one by its library_id, or say they would rather build a new investigator instead (create-investigator).
lines.next: List the library (investigator.list) so the player can choose a card, or use create-investigator for a brand-new one.

campaign.description: filled in automatically from the campaign already being set up

library_id.description: one of the library_id values investigator.list returned

as.description: optional: play this card under a new name, which mints it a row of its own (a second person, not a rename) instead of sharing the original's

lines.do: investigator.load copies the chosen card's sheet into this campaign byte for byte -- no conversion, no re-roll, no era gate (contract §21.3); occupation and point allocation are skipped because the sheet already carries them.
lines.next: Load the investigator: give the library_id to use (from browse-library's list).

lines.do: setup.complete: write the setup_handoff receipt, move the campaign to ready_for_table, exit and print the launch line.
